senses: A flexible rodlike structure that forms the main support of the body in the lowest chordates; a primitive spine.
A similar structure found in the embryos of vertebrates from which the spine develops.
An inhabitant of a planet
An operator of a planetarium
A large nose.
A wild goose.
The process of sperm production in the testes.
A semicircular recess, with stone benches, used as a place for discussion.
A curved bench with a high back.
ety: From Ancient Greek ἐξ (ex, “out of”) + ἕδρα (hédra, “seat”).

senses: A spicy South Indian soup made with tamarind juice.
ety: Probably borrowed from Tamil ரசம் (racam), from Sanskrit रस (rasa, “juice”). Doublet of rasa.

senses: The dye (and former drug) trypan blue.
Slightly fat.
Death due to lack of oxygen.
An acute lack of oxygen.
A gateway to the inner part of an Ancient Egyptian temple.
A pillar used to support a bridge.
A tall steel or concrete tower from which cables are strung.
A lighting mast; a freestanding support for floodlights.
A traffic cone.
ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek πυλών (pulṓn, “gateway”).

senses: The fruit of a citron tree.
The candied rind of the citron fruit.
A greenish yellow colour, inspired by the color of the rind of the citron fruit.
ety: Borrowed from French citron (“lemon, lime”), Latin citrus (“citron tree, thuja”), probably via Etruscan derived from Ancient Greek κέδρος (kédros, “cedar”) (see there for further etymology).

senses: A shapeshifter who can change between cat and human form.
The lowest black belt rank in Japanese martial arts.
One who has attained this rank.
Polydactylous.
ety: From Ancient Greek πολυδάκτυλος (poludáktulos), equivalent to poly- + -dactyl.

senses: Directed social advancement via education and the scientific method.
An orange seedless citrus fruit Citrus unshiu, originating from Japan, about the size of a tangerine.
ety: From Japanese 蜜柑 (ミカン, mikan), short for 温州蜜柑 (うんしゅうミカン, Unshū mikan, literally “honey citrus of Wēnzhōu”).

senses: The author of anarchy; one who excites revolt.
examples: Thus Satan; and him thus the Anarch old / With falt'ring speech and visage incomposed / Answer'd.
As all the world knows, Emma Goldman is the chief anarch of her time.

senses: The seashore, the coast.
examples: Visit the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site in the UK, and ammonite road signs greet you at every town and city and even the lampposts on the seafront feature a familiar coiled shell.

senses: A male Buddhist monk or priest; one who follows all Buddhist precepts as a full member of the sangha.
ety: Transliteration of Pali bhikkhu (“beggar, Buddhist monk”), from Sanskrit भिक्षु (bhikṣu, “mendicant”).

senses: Synonym of monochord (used mainly in reference to ancient Greek music)
ety: From Ancient Greek κᾰνών (kănṓn, “straight rod, bar”). Doublet of cannon, canon, and canyon.

senses: A (normally) complete range.
All the notes in a musical scale.
All the colours that can be presented by a device such as a monitor or printer.
ety: 1520s, original sense “lowest note of musical scale”, contraction of Medieval Latin gamma ut, from gamma (“Greek letter, corresponding to the musical note G”) + ut (“first solfège syllable, now replaced by do”). In modern terms, “G do” – the first note of the G scale. Meaning later extended to mean all the notes of a scale, and then more generally any complete range.

senses: Of, or having, hydrophobia (rabies); rabid.
To arise, issue or emerge; to give rise.
ety: Inherited from Middle English sourden, from Old French sourdre, from Latin surgō, contraction of earlier subrigō. Compare source. Doublet of surge.

senses: Built to be operated out of a seacan, shipping container.

senses: Any of several annual festivals in which Welsh poets, dancers, and musicians compete for recognition.
(more generally) An annual performing arts competition, typically for youth.
ety: Unadapted borrowing from Welsh eisteddfod (“session”), from eistedd (“to sit”) + bod (“to be”), literally “being sitting”.

senses: Able to be ignored.
Insignificant or trivial enough to be ignored.
examples: Users on this Internet chat system are ignorable by right-clicking the user name.

senses: Having hummocks.

A severe psychiatric condition, often associated with schizophrenia, characterized by a tendency to remain in a rigid state of stupor for long periods which give way to short periods of extreme agitation.
A frozen, unresponsive state, as of electronic equipment.
ety: From international scientific vocabulary, from German Katatonie, from New Latin catatonia, from a Greek word meaning to stretch tight. By surface analysis, cata- + tone + -ia.

senses: A person employed to card wool.
A carding machine.
A criminal who steals information from credit cards.
A West African food made from fried mashed cassava tubers.
ety: From Yoruba gàrí, from Hausa gā̀rī.
examples: They cooked together, his mother stirring the soup, Obinze making the garri.

senses: A person who writes the lyrics of a song.
To multiply; to make manifold.
To hold more than one ecclesiastical benefice at the same time.
The state of being a bastard (illegitimate child).
ety: From Middle English bastardrie, an alternation of bastardie after the suffix -erie; equivalent to bastard + -ry.

senses: A side dish (often of vegetables), or a small dish of savories served between courses.
ety: Borrowed from French entremets. Replaced earlier Middle English entermes, from Old French entremés.

senses: Belief in the verifiability principle.
Excessive emphasis on the importance of educational, academic, legal, or regulatory qualifications.
Any of very many chordate marine animals, of the subphyla Tunicata or Urochordata, including the sea squirts.
ety: From translingual Tunicata + -ate (noun-forming suffix). Further from Latin tunicātus, perfect passive participle of tunicō (“to clothe with a tunic”).

senses: A machine that has the ability to terraform.
A person who terraforms.
Someone who orates or delivers an oration.
A skilled and eloquent public speaker.
ety: From Middle English oratour, from Anglo-Norman oratour, from Latin ōrātor.

senses: A person, device or substance that stimulates.
